newsitem.title: USA: Oil tanker strikes bridge, leaks at Portland, Maine.
newsitem.headline: Oil tanker strikes bridge, leaks at Portland, Maine.

text.p: A Liberian-registered tanker struck a drawbridge at Portland, Maine on Friday, damaging the bridge and leaking an unknown amount of oil, a Coast Guard official said.
"It pierced a tank, we're not sure if it's bunker (fuel oil used by the ship itself) or product (cargo)," said Chief Warrant Officer Charles Rathgeber in a telephone interview.

The 560-foot (170-meter) Julie N was entering Portland Harbour with a cargo of 200,000 barrels of No. 2 diesel oil when it struck the Fore River Bridge drawspan, creating a 6-8 foot (1.8-2.4 meter) gash in the vessel's bow two feet (.6 meter) above the waterline, Rathgeber said.
Local and state pollution response teams have set booms, including one seaward of the bridge to keep the oil from spreading into the outer harbour and Casco Bay.
"Fortunately it happened at a slack tide," the Coast Guard official said, explaining that no heavy currents were running to move the oil rapidly.
The bridge between Portland and South Portland was damaged badly enough so that officials opted not to close it pending evaluation.
The Julie N, whose last port of call was New York, is managed by General Ship Services of New York City, according to the latest Coast Guard records available, Rathgeber said.
